next_step.D1: An obituary matches the only owner on title, and the county still shows that person as owner. Read the obituary for the survivors. Check the Clerk's will book index under the decedent's name for a will, a qualification or a List of Heirs (Va. Code 64.2-509). If nothing was filed, the heirs own it by law and all of them must sign.
next_step.D5: Obituaries match every owner named on title. Nobody living is on the deed. The heirs of the last to die usually control the property; start from the later obituary's survivors.
next_step.D4: An obituary matches one of the owners. If the deed gave survivorship (the county's 'A OR B' usually means it did), the survivor owns it outright and only needs to record the death. If it did not, the decedent's share passed to heirs. Pull the deed to see which. The survivor is the person to talk to either way.
